planning_notes: Board is Arduino Mega 2560. Wiring preserved: btn1 signal to D2 (with pullup), servo1 PWM to D3, servo2 PWM to D4; both servos powered from 5V and share GND.1.

Button model: catalog indicates active_high=false and pullup=true, so model 'true' represents a pressed button (i.e., the input is LOW at the MCU while pressed). The digital_input port initial uses the model 'true/false' meaning; on reset the physical button is assumed unpressed, so model starts false (not pressed).
Debouncing and servo alternation (toggle between {servo1=180, servo2=0} and {servo1=0, servo2=180} per press) are SysML business logic; only servo_angle and btn1 digital input ports are created here.
Smooth movement is handled by model timing/update of servo_angle targets; servo smoothness parameters are business-model concerns, not catalog port configuration.

interfaces.name: io_0
interfaces.meaning: btn1 debounced press event (HIGH when pressed per model)

interfaces.name: io_1
interfaces.meaning: servo1 target angle for alternating button-driven position (0<->180)

interfaces.name: io_2
interfaces.meaning: servo2 target angle for alternating button-driven position (180<->0)

configuration_resolution.original_requirement:
Target board is Arduino Mega 2560 as specified in the supplied circuit; use this board when the prose says UNO.


**Task**:
You are tasked with programming an Arduino (uno) to control two servo motors (servo1, servo2) using a push button (btn1). The servos should alternate their positions between 0° and 180° each time the button is pressed. Specifically, when the button is pressed, servo1 should move to 180° and servo2 should move to 0°, and vice versa on the next press.

**Detail Rules**:
Initialization: Upon powering on or resetting, both servos (servo1, servo2) should be set to 0°.
Button Interaction: Each press of the button (btn1) should toggle the positions of the servos. If servo1 is at 0° and servo2 is at 180°, pressing the button should move servo1 to 180° and servo2 to 0°. The next press should reverse their positions again.
Debouncing: The button press should be debounced to avoid false triggers caused by mechanical vibrations.
Servo Movement: The servos should move smoothly to their new positions after each button press.
